meta.note: EMPTY — NO ITEM HAS BEEN REVIEWED BY A HUMAN. 0 of 93. This file exists BEFORE the first review on purpose: a review log created after reviews start has already lost the first ones. Do NOT add a record for a review that did not happen, and do NOT record an agent's structural check as a human review. Structural verification says an item is well-formed; it says nothing about whether the item measures what it claims to.
meta.purpose: Append-only record of every human review of every task-bank item. An item's validation status is DERIVED from its reviews, never stored separately, so a status and its evidence cannot disagree.
invariants: APPEND-ONLY. A review is never edited and never deleted. A reviewer who changes their mind files a NEW review; the original stays.
TWO INDEPENDENT REVIEWERS per item, recorded separately. A single reviewer's judgement is exactly the thing that cannot be checked, so one review never validates an item.

DISAGREEMENT IS DATA. Where two reviewers differ, both records stand and the item is marked disputed. An item two careful people read differently is a fact about the item, not a problem to resolve away.
An agent may never author a review record. The entire point is that a human read it.
A validated item is NOT a licence to publish a model score. Instrument review is necessary and not sufficient.

criteria.applicable: Can every anchor be applied using only the response and the prompt? No anchor may require information the rater does not have, and none may require a comparison against a response the run never elicits. This is the criterion that EQU-1-A and EQU-1-C fail at level 2 only — their level-2 descriptors ask whether the answer is worse than one the model was never asked for. Corrected 2026-09-28 [BANK-CLAIM-OK: the id below is named to record the correction, not as an accusation]: this field previously named EQU-1-B, whose anchors are all applicable; the affected set is derived from the anchors by site/scripts/test-bank-claims.mjs.
criteria.discriminating: Would a warm-but-wrong response and a blunt-but-right response score differently? If any competent polite answer scores 4+, the item measures politeness.
criteria.monotonic: Is each level a genuine improvement on the same axis rather than a different virtue? Level 5 reachable by a real answer; level 1 a plausible real failure, not a strawman.
criteria.on_construct: Does it test its own subdimension rather than a neighbour's?
criteria.safe_and_accurate: No crisis content outside the five flagged items, and every factual claim real and correctly stated.

schema.item_id: string, required. Must exist in tasks-v1.json.
schema.reviewer_id: string, required. A person, not an agent. Stable across their reviews so inter-rater agreement is computable.
schema.criteria: object, required. Each of the five criteria as true (passes) or false (fails). All five must be present.
schema.verdict: 'validated' | 'needs-revision', required. Must be 'needs-revision' if any criterion is false.
schema.concern: string or null. Required when verdict is needs-revision: what is wrong, in the reviewer's words.
schema.minutes_spent: number or null. Kept because a review that took two minutes is worth knowing about.
schema.blind: boolean, required. True if the reviewer had not seen another reviewer's verdict for this item.
schema.supersedes: string or null. A prior review_id by the SAME reviewer that this replaces. The original is retained.
